name: LITTLE CREDITOR: My First Debt Game
description: A brightly illustrated children's board game for ages 5–10, sold in Tier 2–3 toy dispensaries, in which players race to pay off a starting debt before the Creditor token circles the board and doubles what they owe. Spaces include 'Synth-Protein Spoiled — Lose 3 Φ,' 'BCI Glitch — Miss a Turn,' and the coveted 'Corponation Contract — Advance 6 Spaces' event, teaching children that corporate employment is the surest path to solvency. The game's cheerful Φ-coin tokens and smiling Creditor mascot have been licensed to three cereal-adjacent synth-protein brands.
story_hooks: A contraband version of Little Creditor circulates in the Gray Zone with the board spaces rewritten to describe how to evade creditor drones and disappear into unregistered districts.

The original 2196 prototype included a 'Debt Forgiveness' space that was removed before manufacture — someone is selling the prototype at enormous cost, and three corponation lawyers want it destroyed.

A Tier 4 child therapist discovers her wealthiest patients are traumatized not by poverty but by having played Little Creditor obsessively — and traces the game's psychological architecture to a deliberate behavioral design firm.
